prompt.es: Resuelve el caso: escribe el informe para el comité.

answer.text: Incident report: flood in the basement. Prepared for the committee. At six o'clock, according to the caretaker, a pipe burst in the basement. By midnight, the water had reached the shelves, and most of the equipment had been ruined. The alarm had not gone off. The basement is used every week by the youth club, so the loss is serious. The caretaker says he sent a message to the committee at seven; apparently, nobody read it until the next morning, although this has not been confirmed. Had the alarm worked, the volunteers would have arrived in time and moved the equipment upstairs. If the message had been read on Friday evening, the damage would have been much smaller. However, it would be unfair to blame one person: the alarm allegedly failed last year too, and nobody checked it. Would the committee consider installing a second alarm and asking the volunteers to check it every month? I also suggest that the caretaker keep a written list of calls, and I recommend that the committee act quickly. Revision note: I replaced the kids with the children in the first draft, changed this to this delay so the reference is clear, and moved the proposal to the end because the committee reads the facts first.

Incident report for the committee. According to the caretaker, a pipe burst at six o'clock in the basement. By midnight, the water had already reached the shelves, and much of the equipment had been ruined. The alarm had not gone off. Apparently, the caretaker sent a message at seven, but nobody read it until Saturday; this has not been confirmed. Had the alarm worked, the volunteers would have moved the equipment upstairs in time. If someone had read the message, the damage would have been smaller. We suggest that the committee install a second alarm and that the volunteers check it every month. Would it be possible to keep a list of calls as well? Revision: I replaced the kids with the children, added this delay instead of this, and cut two long phrases to make the report more concise.
